mya: akimaayotaakani pyaaki, oowaaha naapi kati išiliniyani mihtahkionki naapi leni iišinaakwahki kiišikonki.
en: Thy kingdom come, thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.

mya: miililoome noonki kaahkiihkwe niwaawinaakaneminaani, neehi wanipiilakiilo niiloona mahsenahamaanki,
en: Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our debts, as we forgive what others owe us.

mya: iši niiloona weenipiilakiaanki mahsenahamawiyaminciki. aapooši wiihkata awašihsooloome meeleewahki išiliniaanki, ateehši šiikwihiloome meeleewahkinkonci.
en: Also lead us not into evil, but free us from evil.

mya: wiihsakacaakwa ihsa weekici. awiiwali ihsa eehsaaci.
en: Wiihsakacaakwa was living at a place. He had a wife.

mya: neehi-hsa kapootwe awiihkaanali neewaapamaaci oonsaanikwali. neehi-hsa eehšamekoci wiina.
en: Once, he went to see his friend Fox Squirrel. Then he was fed nut meats.

mya: neehi-hsa, “awatoolo!” iilinci. “kiniicaanhsaki awatawi”, iilinci iihkwihtankia.
en: “Take some!” he was told. “Take the leftovers back to your children”, he was told.

mya: “naapiši-hkwa, niihka, naapi teehtawi meeciaanki.” neehi-hsa,
en: “Just like this, my friend, we eat stuff just like this”. And then (Wiihsakacaakwa told Fox Squirrel) “You must come and visit me.”

mya: “nawi kiiwikawiihkani.” neehi-hsa oonsaanikwa keewikawici. neewaapamaaci awiihkaanali.
en: And so Fox Squirrel went visiting. He went to see his friend.

mya: “piintikiilo, niihka! ciinkweepilo!” neehi-hsa-hka ahšamaaci wiina. aalweelici poohkišanki awiiyawi. naahpa-hsa teehši niihpikani seekihkaaki. wiina-hka siikihkaakipa. peekwaaci poohkahanki awiiyawi. meekwika taani iilaapankiici iišilenita. aalweelici. neehi-hsa aalweelici ahšamaaci wiina. aapweelici eehkwi awiila ahšamaahsiikwi wiihsakacaakwa.
en: (Wiihsakacaakwa told Fox Squirrel) “Come in, my friend! Sit down!” Then (Wiihsakacaakwa) tried to feed him nut meats. He couldn’t cut a hole in himself. But instead, blood just poured out. Nut meats were supposed to pour out. He gouged himself for no good reason. He would try anything he saw anyone else doing, and he would fail. And so, he failed to feed him nut meats (Fox Squirrel) went back home when Wiihsakacaakwa could not feed him.

mya: neehi-hsa “awiihkaanali nawaapamaka”, iilaaci awiiwali. “ninkwiilotaaswi”. mahkooli niiši keewikawici.
en: Then, “I’m going to see (Fox Squirrel’s) friend”, (Wiihsakacaakwa) told his wife, “I’m lonely” He went to visit Bear.

mya: “piiwa niihkaana wiihsakacaakwa!” iilikoci-hsa awiihkaanali mahkooli, “piintikiilo, niihka! wilenaahkiilo”, iilaaci awiiwali, “eehi ciinkweepici kati niihkaana wiihsakacaakwa”. neehi-hsa, “keetwi kati ahšamankwi kiilimwa? alemihkapilo!” iilaaci awiiwali mahkwa.
en: (Bear said) “Here comes my friend Wiihsakacaakwa!” His friend Bear said to (Wiihsakacaakwa) “Come in, my friend! Spread something out where my friend Wiihsakacaakwa can sit”, he told his wife. And then (Bear said to his wife): “What shall we feed your brother-in-law? Turn around!”, Bear told his wife.

mya: neehi-hsa mayaawi waapankiici wiihsakacaakwa iišilenilici. neehihsa ahkaawi peehkišamawaata awiiwali. neehi-hsa keešisamoonci, eehšamenci.
en: And then Wiihsakacaakwa closely watched what (Bear) did. (Bear) cut the tenderloin out of his wife. And then, when it was done being cooked for him, (Wiihsakacaakwa) was fed with it.

mya: neehi-hsa mahkwa atoontani poohkahanki. pimi seekihkaaki. neehi-hsa eehšamaaci awiihkaanali ahkaawi neehi pimi.
en: Then Bear pierced her heel. Grease poured out. And so (Bear) fed his friend tenderloin and grease.

mya: neehi-hsa, “awatoolo iihkwihtamania!” iilinci wiihsakacaakwa. “neepa-hka miiciwaki kiniicaanhsaki.”
en: “Take your leftovers with you”, Wiihsakacaakwa was told. “Maybe your children will eat it.”

mya: “ho! naapiši-hkwa niila, naapiši naapi teehtawi meeciaanki, niihka”.
en: “Ho! Just like this, as for myself, we eat stuff just like this, my friend”.

mya: neehi-hsa naapiši, “nawaapamiihkaanke niihka!” iilaaci mahkooli wiihsakacaakwa. neehi-hsa maacaaci.
en: And then, in the same way, “Come and see us, my friend”, Wiihsakacaakwa said to Bear. Then (Wiihsakacaakwa) headed home.

mya: neehi-hsa noonki mahkwa aašite keewikawici.
en: Then it was Bear’s turn to come visit.

mya: “ho! niihkaana piiwa mahkwa! wilenaahkawi”, iilaaci awiiwali, “eehi-hka ciinkweepici.” neehi-hsa: “piintikiilo, niihka!” iilaaci mahkooli. neehi-hsa ceenkweepici.
en: “Ho! Here comes my friend Bear! Let’s spread something out where he can sit down”, (Wiihsakacaakwa) said to his wife. “Come in, my friend!” he said to Bear. And then he sat down.

mya: “keetwi kati ahšamankwi kiilimwa?” iilaaci-hsa awiiwali. “meeneehwiki kiikoo kati ahšamankwi. maalhsi miililo!” iilaaci awiiwali.
en: “What shall we feed your brother-in-law?” (Wiihsakacaakwa) asked his wife. “There isn’t anything to feed him with. Give me a knife!” he said to his wife.

mya: “keetwi kati ihpenatooyani?” iilikoci awiiwali. leni peekwananka kati ahšamaaci.
en: “What are you going to do with it?” his wife asked him. She apparently didn’t know what he was going to feed him.

mya: “alemihkapilo!” iilaaci-hsa awiiwali.
en: Turn around!” he said to his wife.

mya: “keetwi-hka išiliniyani?”
en: “What are you going to do?”

mya: “ciinkweepilo! alemihkapilo!”
en: “Sit down! Turn around!”

mya: neehi-hsa kahsilišwaaci apahkaaminki awiiwali ahkaawi kati pahkišanki. neehi-hsa seehseehkašwaaci peehkišanki ahkaawi. meehci peehkišanki mahkwa pinkwi eensinanki niiyaaha eehkwaahkiici eehi pahkišanki. neehi-hsa šiišonanki pinkwi. aapwe kiipoohwiki eehonci pahkišanki awiiwali ahkaawi. aalweelici-hsa kati ahšamaaci awiihkaanali, aapwe ihsa eehšantanki awiiyawi.
en: And he cut into his wife’s back, so as to cut out her tenderloin. And she cried and cried as (Wiihsakacaakwa) cut out her tenderloin. After he cut it out, Bear gathered up ashes and tossed them there where (Wiihsakacaakwa) had cut it out. Then he rubbed in the ashes. It healed back up from where he had cut out his wife’s tenderloin. (Wiihsakacaakwa) failed to feed his friend, he just fed himself again.

mya: “taani ciikhši iišileniyani, niihka?” iilikoci mahkooli.
en: “How did you do it, my friend?” Bear asked.

mya: “naapi-hkwa išiliniaani iiši ahšamiyani.”
en: “I did it the same way as you fed me!”

mya: neehi-hsa mahkwa maacaaci.
en: And so Bear went home.

mya: neehi-hsa noohki waapanki aapooši neewaapamaaci awiihkaanali kwaahkwali.
en: And the next day, (Wiihsakacaakwa) again went off, to visit his friend Woodpecker.

mya: “piiwa niihkaana wiihsakacaakwa. wilenaahkawi eehi-hka ciinkweepici”, iilaaci kwaahkwa awiiwali. “piintikiilo, niihka! ciinkweepilo, niihka!” iilinci wiihsakacaakwa neehi wiihsa kwaahkwa aniicaanhsahi. neehi-hsa “noonki keetwi-hka ahšamankwi kiilimwa wiihsakacaakwa?” neehi-hsa kwaahkwa awiiwali: “alikonci wilenaahkiilo ciika tawaani caacinkilaakia.”
en: “Here comes my friend Wiihsakacaakwa! Spread something out where he can sit down”, Woodpecker said to his wife. “Come in, my friend! Sit down, my friend!”, Wiihsakacaakwa was told (by Woodpecker) and Woodpecker’s many children. And then, “Now what will we feed your brother-in-law Wiihsakacaakwa?” Then Woodpecker said to his wife: “Spread something out over yonder near the shagbark hickory tree”.

mya: neehi-hsa weelaantaweeci tawaani kwaahkwa. neehi-hsa kwaahkohkwia tawaani alaakani, weelaantaweeta kwaahkwa saahsikawahi peenahwaaci. “naahpa-hsa waapisici moohsiahi, saahsikawaki”, iilaaci wiihsakacaakwali eehšamaaci.
en: And so Woodpecker climbed up the tree. Then as Woodpecker’s wife (held a) wooden dish, Woodpecker climbed up and knocked down cracklings. “Instead of grub worms, (we should feed him) cracklings”, that’s how (Woodpecker) told (his wife) to feed Wiihsakacaakwa.

mya: “wiihsinilo, niihka! keetwi-hka eehšamelaani? ooniini-hkwa teehši niiloona meeciaanki. iihkwihtamani awatoolo piloohsaki. miiciwaki kiniicaanhsaki”.
en: “Eat, my friend, what shall I feed you?” (he said to Wiihsakacaakwa). “This is the only thing we eat. Take along your leftovers to the children. Your children will eat it”.

mya: “naapiši weehsiniaanki naapi teehtawi meeciaanki”, iilaaci kwaahkwali. neehi-hsa maacaata wiihsakacaakwa. neehi-hsa: “nawaapamiihkani niihka!” iilaaci kwaahkwali.
en: We eat the same stuff, we eat it”, (Wiihsakacaakwa) said to kwaahkwali. neehi-hsa maacaata wiihsakacaakwa. neehi-hsa: Woodpecker. And then, Wiihsakacaakwa headed for home. And he said to Woodpecker, “You must come and see me, my friend”.

mya: neehi-hsa neewaapamekoci kwaahkwali.
en: And so Woodpecker came to visit (Wiihsakacaakwa).

mya: neehi-hsa wiihsakacaakwa maacaaci. neehi-hsa tawaani keehkišanki aapweeyaaci. eehkwa pampaalici weelišanki tawaani. kwaahkwaki ahkiwana naapiilišanki tawaani.
en: And so Wiihsakacaakwa headed off. And he was carving a stick as he returned. As he walked along, he carved the stick. He was carving woodpecker bills out of the stick.

mya: neehi-hsa šayiipaawe niiyaaha aawiki pyaalici awiihkaanali kwaahkwali. neehi-hsa naapihšikoleewaaci aniicaanhsahi, neehi awiiwali, neehi awiila. naapihšikoleehowaaci.
en: Then, in the morning, his friend Woodpecker arrived there. They stuck them onto their noses, his children, and his wife, and himself. They put them on their noses.

mya: neehi-hsa “niihkaana piiwa kwaahkwa!” iilaaci awiiwali. “wilenaahkawi kati ciinkweepiwa! “piintikiilo, niihka! ciinkweepilo! aalimiihtoohsiiwani?” iilaaci awiiwali.
en: “My friend Woodpecker is coming!” he said to his wife. Spread something out where he can sit down! Come in, my friend! Sit down! Aren’t you going to cook something?” he said to his wife.

mya: “keetwi-hka niihi peehkahamaani?”
en: “What will I put on to cook, then?”

mya: “alikonci tawaani ciika wilenaahkiilo.”
en: “Over yonder near the tree, spread something out”.

mya: neehi-hsa weelaantaweeci tawaani. “alaakani piitoolo!” iilaaci awiiwali. neehi peepakantanki tawaani kiicintasitooki ahkiwanenki. neehi paapincinki. niihpikani noonteehtanki ahkiwanenkonci.
en: And so (Wiihsakacaakwa) climbed up the tree. “Bring a dish!”, he said to his wife. Then he pecked at the tree, to push the fake bill onto his nose. Then he fell down. Blood was running from his nose.

mya: neehi-hsa awiila kwaahkwa noonteehsaaci. seehsiikihkaawaaci saahsikawaki. neehi-hsa aapwe awiila eehšamaaci awiihkaanali.
en: Then Woodpecker ran out. The cracklings poured out. And then he fed his friend in return.

mya: wiihsakacaakwa: “naapi-hkwa iišileniaampa, naahpa noonki nintaalweeli. keetoohkwe iilohkiwiaani?” neehi-hsa maacaaci aapwe kwaahkwa.
en: Wiihsakacaakwa said: “I used to do things this way, but now I fail. What’s wrong with me?” And so Woodpecker went back home.

mya: neehi-hsa: “aapooši noohki ninawaapamaa kati niihkaana amehkwa.”
en: And then Wiihsakacaakwa said, “I’m going to visit my friend Beaver next”.

mya: neehi-hsa “piiwa kiilimwa!” iilaata awiiwali. “wilenaahkawi eehihka ciinkweepici! “piintikiilo, niihka! ciinkweepilo!” iilikota awiihkaanali amehkwali. “kiilimwa keetwi kati ahšamankwi? ahkihkwi akatoolo!” iilaaci awiiwali amehkwa.
en: “Here comes your brother-in-law!”, (Beaver) said to his wife. “Spread out something where he can sit down! Come in, my friend! Sit down!” Beaver said to his friend. “What will we feed your brother-in-law? Hang up the kettle!”, Beaver said to his wife.

mya: neehi-hsa nkoti akwihsali weehkamaaci. neehi-hsa eenkihaaci akwihsali. neehi peehkahwaata aniicaanhsali. neehi eehšamenci wiihsakacaakwa amehkoonsali.
en: And he called in one of his sons. And he killed his son. Then he put him on to cook. And Wiihsakacaakwa was fed with the young beaver.

mya: “waaha, niihka, ahtoohkani ahkana ceeki mihtekwilaakanenki”. neehi-hsa ceeki niiyaaha eehtooki ahkana. nkoti eekwaleentanki.
en: “My friend, put all the bones here in the wooden dish.” Then he put all the bones there. He kept one in his mouth.

mya: neehi awiila amehkwa nawi seekaahkiita ahkana siipionkiši. neehi noonki weehkamaaci akwihsali. “pyaalo, amehkoonse!” iilaaci. naahpa aapwe pyaalici seehkweelici. “keetwi iišinaakosiyani? taaniši, niihka, iihpinatawiyani niniicaanhsa? nkoti aanihkwikanki atapihšinihkiaakani meeneehwiki!”
en: Then Beaver went to the river to throw the bones out. Then he called up his son. “Come, little beaver!” he said. But (the little Beaver) came back weeping. (Then Beaver said to his son) “What is wrong with you?” (Then, to Wiihsakacaakwa,) “My friend, what have you done to hurt my child? One joint of his little finger is missing!”

mya: neehi-hsa wiihsakacaakwa neenatonanki atooninki. neehi-hsa meehkonanka, noontiaahkiici. aapwe miilaaci awiihkaanali.
en: Wiihsakacaakwa felt around in his mouth. He found it and took it out. He gave it back to his friend.

mya: neehi-hsa maacaata. awiihkaanali: “nawaapamiihkani, niihka!” iilaaci. neehi-hsa maacaaci wiihsakacaakwa.
en: And (Wiihsakacaakwa) started home. To his friend, Beaver, he said “come and visit me sometime”. Then Wiihsakacaakwa left.

mya: neehi-hsa amehkwa neewaapamaaci awiihkaanali.
en: So then Beaver went to visit his friend (Wiihsakacaakwa).

mya: “niihkaana piiwa amehkwa! wilenaahkawi eehi-hka ciinkweepici!” iilaaci awiiwali wiihsakacaakwa. “piintikiilo! ciinkweepilo, niihka! pootaweelo! aalimiihtawaahsiiwani kiilimwa amehkwa?”
en: “Here comes my friend Beaver! Let’s spread something out where he can sit down”, Wiihsakacaakwa said to his wife. “Come in, sit down, my friend! Make a fire! Aren’t you going to cook something for your brother-in-law Beaver?

mya: “keetwi-hka eehšamankwi?”
en: “What shall we feed him?”

mya: neehi-hsa ahkihkwi eekatooki mitemohsa. meehci nipi weenteeki, weehkamaaci akwihsali, “wiihsakacaakoonhse!”
en: So the woman hung up the kettle. Once the water was boiling, he called for his son, Young Wiihsakacaakwa.

mya: “keetwi kati išiliniyani?” šaaye leni-hkwa peekwananki iišileninki.
en: “What are you going to do?” It was as if she didn’t know what was going to be done.

mya: neehi-hsa eenkihaata akwihsali. neehi peehkahwaaci. eehkwi kiihkiihkišwaaci akwihsali, seeseehkwiyohkaatiici awiiwali. “ninkwihsa, ninkwihsa”, iici. seehkweeci. “nko-hka noohki neewaki ninkwihsa.”
en: Then (Wiihsakacaakwa) killed his son, and put him on to cook. While he cut up his son, his wife cried and cried. “My son, my son”, she said. She cried. “I’ll never see my son again”.

mya: neehi-hsa eehšamaaci awiihkaanali amehkwali. neehi-hsa tawaani alaakani niiyaaha eehtooki. “niiyaaha ahkana ahtoohkani, niihka,” iilaaci amehkwali. neehi-hsa nipinkiši peekitanki. neehihsa: “antomi kikwihsina!” iilaaci awiiwali.
en: And so (Wiihsakacaakwa) fed his friend Beaver. And he set down a wooden plate there. “Put the bones there, my friend”, he said to Beaver. And he threw (the bones) away into the water. And then he said to his wife, “Call our son!”

mya: mitemohsa seehkweeci. aalweelici weehkamaaci.
en: The woman was weeping. She couldn’t call him.

mya: neehi-hsa pyaahsiilikwi. neehi-hsa amehkwa weehkamaaci. neehihsa piihsaalici noonki akwihsali. noonki maacaaci amehkwa.
en: So he did not come. Then Beaver called him. His son came running up now. Then Beaver went home.

mya: neehi-hsa noonki noohki waapanki neewaapamaaci kihkamanhsiali.
en: And now the next day, (Wiihsakacaakwa) went to see Kingfisher.

mya: “piiwa niihkaana wiihsakacaakwa! wilenaahkawi eehi ciinkweepici!” iilaaci awiiwali. “piintikiilo! ciinkweepilo, niihka! pootaweelo! ahkihkwi akotoolo! keetwi-hka niihi eehšamankwi?”
en: (Kingfisher) said to his wife, “Here comes my friend Wiihsakacaakwa! Spread something out where he can sit down. Come in, sit down, my friend! Make a fire! Hang the kettle up! What shall we feed him, then?”

mya: neehi-hsa siipionkiši iiyaaci kihkamanhsia. neehi-hsa kiihkoneehsali neetomaata. neehi-hsa kinoošiali pyaalici. neehihsa kihkamanhsia ceemonkihsaaci. seekiinaaci. neehi-hsa saakaciolaata kinoošiali. peehkahwaaci. neehi-hsa eehšamenci wiihsakacaakwa.
en: And so Kingfisher went to the river. He called a fish. A pike came. Kingfisher dropped into the water. He caught (the pike). Then he pulled (the pike) ashore. He put him on to cook. Then Wiihsakacaakwa was fed.

mya: iintaahswi iihkohpwaaci, “awatawaahkani kiniicaanhsaki! neepahka eemwaaciki kiihkoneehsali.
en: Of what he had left, (Kingfisher) said, “Take it along to your children. Maybe they will eat the fish

mya: “naapiši weehsiniaanki, niihka. aašite nawaapamiihkani, niihka!” iilaaci kihkamanhsiali. neehi-hsa wiihsakacaakwa maacaaci. neehihsa waapanki kihkamanhsia neewaapamaaci wiihsakacaakwali.
en: “We eat the same thing, my friend. You must come and see me next, my friend”, (Wiihsakacaakwa) said to Kingfisher. So then Wiihsakacaakwa went home. The next day Kingfisher visited Wiihsakacaakwa.

mya: neehi-hsa waapeekinkia naanaapihkamohaaci aniicaanhsahi, neehi awiiwali, neehi awiila. neehi: “piiwa niihkaana kihkamanhsia! wilenaahkawi eehi-hka ciinkweepici!” iilaaci awiiwali. neehi: “piintikiilo! ciinkweepilo, niihka!”, iilaaci kihkamanhsiali. “aalimiihtoolo!”
en: And (Wiihsakacaakwa) tied white cloths around the necks of his children, and his wife, and himself. Then he said to his wife, “Here comes my friend Kingfisher. Let’s spread something out where he can sit down”. And then: “Come in! Sit down, my friend!”, he said to Kingfisher. “Cook something!” (he said to his wife).

mya: šaawe awiiwali seekisilici. “keetwi-hka peehkahamaani?”
en: Right away, his wife became scared. “What will I put on to cook?”

mya: “pootaweelo! ahkihkwi akotoolo!” iilaaci awiiwali.
en: “Make a fire! Hang up the kettle!” Wiihsakacaakwa told his wife.

mya: neehi noonki noonteehsaaci nawi weehkamaaci kiihkoneehsali. kinoošiali pyaalici. niišiihsaaci-hka sakiinaaci. kiihkoneehsa taawaletoneehsaata. neehi-hsa wiihsakacaakwa kweentikoci.
en: And then (Wiihsakacaakwa) ran out to call up a fish. A pike came. (Wiihsakacaakwa) jumped there, trying to catch him. The fish came with its mouth open. And so Wiihsakacaakwa was swallowed up.

mya: teepilekahkwi. neehi-hsa awiiwali seekisilici. seehkweelici. “niilimwe, taaniši toke iilohkiwici? aayaahkamehkaawa!”
en: Time passed. Then his wife became frightened. She wept. “Brotherin-law, what can have become of (Wiihsakacaakwa)? He is gone forever!” (she said to Kingfisher).

mya: neehi-hsa siipionkiši iihsaaci kihkamanhsia. neehi-hsa eentomaaci kiihkoneehsali. aapwe-hsa pyaalici, eehinkaaha wiihsakacaakwa kweentikocili.
en: And then Kingfisher rushed over to the river. Then he called up the fish. One came back over to him, the same one who had swallowed Wiihsakacaakwa.

mya: neehi-hsa kihkamanhsia seekiinaaci, saakaciolaata. neehihsa poohkiciišwaaci. neepa-hsa niiyaaha ceenkweepici moonihkialileeta wiihsakacaakwa. iini wiiyoonkonci mihšimaalhsaki waahsipikihkiiwaaci.
en: And then Kingfisher caught (the fish), and took it out of the water. He cut open (the fish’s) belly. But Wiihsakacaakwa was sitting there with his hair all rotted off. That’s why white men have bald heads.

mya: neehi-hsa teekweewiteeheeci. neehi-hsa kiipahwaaci aniicaanhsahi masaanikaanionki. neehi “waapamihsooko!” iilaaci aniicaanhsahi neehi awiiwali. “nintekweewiteehee. kinakalelimwa kati.” maaciihkaaci peminkiši. “waapamihsooko!” iilaaci aniicaanhsahi neehi awiiwali.
en: And so (Wiihsakacaakwa) felt ashamed. Then he locked his children in a tent. “Don’t look at me!”he said to his children and wife. “I’m ashamed of myself. I’m going to leave you all.” (Wiihsakacaakwa) headed up towards the sky. “Don’t look at me!”, he said to his children and wife.

mya: neehi-hsa awiiwali: “keetwi toki kati išilinita?” iišiteeheeci mitemohsa. neehi kiimi eekohsenanki masaanikaani. waapamaaci anaapeemali.
en: “I wonder what he’s going to do?” his wife thought. And she secretly raised the tent. She watched her husband.

mya: naahpa-hsa peminkiši iiyaalici. neehi-hsa aapwe paapincinki. neehi-hsa kaakipakwi poohkancionki peentikiihsaaci tawaaninki meehcaahkwahki. iiniini-hsa wiiyoonkonci wiihsakacaakwa iilinci. moošaki taani iilaapankiici iišilenici.
en: But he went upwards. Then he fell back. And then he fell into some leaves in a big hollow tree. It’s for that reason that Wiihsakacaakwa got his name. He always did like he saw others do.

mya: neehi-hsa: “eehkwi kati ašiihkiwi pimaamihkihsinki, alenia eehkwi mihtohseeniwici, kati nintaayaacimekooki noohsemaki, nintaayaalhsoohkaalikooki.”
en: And then (Wiihsakacaakwa said)“As long as the earth endures and as long as man is alive, my grandchildren will talk about me, and tell stories about me.”

mya: eehinki eehkwaapiikaasici.
en: That’s as far as (the story) goes.

mya: wilakhtwaaalaahšaaci wilakhtwa. awiiwali eewalaaci ahkihkwi meehšaaki, tawaani kookani, kitahsaakani, alenaswa-pimi.
en: The Story of WilakhtwaWilakhtwa was out on a long hunt. He brought along his wife, and a big kettle, a wooden spoon, some parched corn, and some beef tallow.

mya: neehi-hsa aalimiihtooki. neehi-hsa antopaliahi pyaalici. neehi-hsa kitahsaakani peehkahanki. neehi-hsa šaaye naawi meehtiteeki kašiki-pimi peehkahanki. neehi-hsa noontawaaci antopaliahi peepiikinekaalikoci. “piintikiiko! ciinkweepiko! eehkwa paala. wiihsiniihkaawi, neehi kati kiwiiteemilemwa.”
en: Once he was cooking. And some warriors were coming. And so he put the parched corn on to boil. And when it was almost done, he put some of the tallow in the water to boil. Then he heard the warriors give the war whoop. “Come in! Sit down! Hold on a bit, please. We should eat, then I’ll go with you.”

mya: neehi-hsa kiišaaphkiteeki kitahsaakanaapowi eeyoowakinci, eewaniinkweeswaata ceeki, neehi šaahšaakahwaata.
en: And then, he threw the hot corn soup at them, blinding them all. Then he beat them to death.

mya: neehi-hsa noohki kotakahi pyaalici ceekalaalici eenkihaaci. neehihsa pihkwaahkionkiši iiyaaci. neehi-hsa pyaalici antopaliahi. neehi awiiwali eewatoonci seekiinamoonci. seehseehkwawalinci awiiwali. kiihkeelintanka eewalenci.
en: And then, again, some more people were coming, on the side of those who he had killed. Then he went up on a hill. And then the warriors arrived. Then his wife was seized and taken away. His wife was led away crying. (Wilakhtwa) knew that she was being taken away.

mya: neehi-hsa alenasooli eenkihaaci. neehi-hsa apihkwayi neehpikinanki. neehi-hsa eetehtolenici. niiyaaha miiyonki taahtakiihšinki, eehi-hka peempaalilici.
en: And so (Wilakhtwa) killed a buffalo. And then he put blood on the bladder. Then he put it on his head like a hat. He then laid down there on the road where (the warriors) were about to pass by.

mya: neehi-hsa meehkohkaakoci antopaliahi. ciikaahkwe waapamekoci. neehi-hsa peesikwiihsaaci, keewineeci. ceeki seekihaaci. neehi neehkimwiilici, ceeki eenkihaaci.
en: And so the warriors found him. They examined him closely. Then, he quickly jumped up and let out a groan. He scared them all. They fainted, and he killed them all.

mya: neehi awiiwali eewalaaci aapwe maacaata. neehi-hsa neehpyaaci neepiki. neehi-hsa weelihsenci. neeyakonakahki aapwe paanahonci, naahpa meeneehwici. teehši poohkahki ašiihkiwi eehi ahsenci.
en: Then he took his wife and started heading back. Then, when (Wilakhtwa) got there, he died. He was buried. Four days later he was dug back up, but he was gone. Instead, there was just a hole in the ground where he had been put.

mya: eehinki eehkwaapiikaasici.
en: That’s as far as he goes.

mya: paapankamwa aalhsoohkaakanipaapankamwa peempaalici neehi kiimoteci pimi. meehci kiimoteci amiihsitonaakanahi meehkaayonaaci.
en: Fox was walking around, and he stole some grease. After he stole it, he used it to grease his whiskers.

mya: neehi-hsa mahweewali aašitehkawaaci. “keetwi iihši meeciyani? meehkaawitonani.”
en: Then he met up with wolf. “What have you been eating, little brother? Your mouth is all greasy.”

mya: neehi-hsa: “alikonci eekotenki. kiila iihpisiyani-hka teepihsaayani”.
en: Then fox said: “It’s hanging over there. You should be tall enough to reach it.”

mya: “pimi niiyaašilo, iihši.”
en: “Take me to the grease, little brother.”

mya: “ooniini eekotenki pimi”, iilaaci ahseensali mahweewali. mahweewa eempihsaaci. neehi-hsa poohkantanki ašihsayi waawaapiihkiciaki. neehi šeehšahakota miisaahaki antepikaninki. neehi paapankamwa keeweešinawaaci ahseensali. neehi maacaamwita cilahkionkiši.
en: “The grease is hung up here”, (fox) said to his older brother wolf. Then wolf jumped up. Then he bit a hole in the hornets’ nest. And they stung (wolf) all over his head. And fox laughed at his older brother. Then he ran away into the brush.

mya: aapooši meehkohkawaata ahseensali. neelapaalayohseeci paapankamwa. kiimoteci kiihkoneehsahi eenswaholaaci. soonkacilici neelapihsaalici ansooyinki kiihpilaaci.
en: And once again, (wolf) met up with his older brother. Fox was walking along with his tail rattling. He had stolen some fish and tied them together. They had frozen solid, and they rattled where he had tied them on his tail.

mya: aašitehkawaaci ahseensali. neehi-hsa “taaniši iišileniyani iihši, seekiinaci kiihkoneehsinsaki?” iilikoci ahseensali mahweewali.
en: Then (fox) met up with his older brother. Then his older brother wolf asked him, “What did you do, little brother, to catch all these little fish?”

mya: “aašoohkooni poohkahamaani, ceemonkaalaweepiaani waapanwi”, iilaaci. noonki ahseensali weenimaaci.
en: “I cut a hole in the ice and sat down and stuck my tail in it all night”, he said to him. He fooled his older brother then.

mya: neehi-hsa mahweewa aašoohkooninki poohkahanka. ceemonkaalaweepici waapanwi, kati kiihkoneehsinsahi sakiinaaci. naapa-hsa aašitatinki ansooyi. aalweelici kati saakaciweeci. neehihsa šaahšaakahakoci mihšimaalhsali.
en: And so wolf made a hole in the ice. And he sat and stuck his tail in it til morning, in order to catch the little fish. And then his tail froze in the ice. He couldn’t get out. And then he was clubbed to death by a white man.

mya: neehi-hsa aayaahkami maacaamwici paapankamwa. eehkwa piici niiyaaha wiiyaahkiita.
en: Then fox ran away for good. He’s probably there still.

mya: eehinki eehkwaapiikasita.
en: That’s as far as he goes.

mya: waapanswa eehi wiikici. neehi-hsa ciikaahkwe nalaaohki-alenaswa, neehi mitemohsaki ciikaahkwe weekiwaaci niišwi.
en: Rabbit was living at a place. And nearby was a buffalo, and two women lived nearby as well.

mya: neehi-hsa waapanswa neewaapamaaci mitemohsahi naanaasihkawaaci. nalaaohki-alenaswa naapiši neewaapamaaci. kapootwe-hsa meehkohkaatiiwaaci waapanswa neehi alenaswa eehi mitemohsaki wiikiwaaci. neehi-hsa kyaaweentiiwaaci. waapanswa: “niila nintaya!”, iilaaci mitemohsahi alenasooli. neehi-hsa ceešikiteeta maacaaci.
en: Rabbit went to visit the women, to court them. Buffalo also went to visit them. Soon rabbit and buffalo met up with each other where the women lived. They became jealous of each other. The rabbit said to the women about the buffalo: “That’s my animal!” And so he went home angry.

mya: neehi-hsa kati nayekoci alenasooli. “niila nintaya iinaana kiinšiwa niiši išiteeheeyiikwe, oowaaha pimihsaahaka”, iilaaci ihsa mitemohsahi waapanswa. neehi-hsa naapiinkwiaakani neetotamaakiici, neehi-hsa paapakiciikaakana, neehi-hsa nihsepikaakani teehtipaapiikiinki alenaswayi. neehi-hsa wiiwaši neetotamaakiici. neehi-hsa noonki weelaholaaci. neehi-hsa paapakiciikaakana weelahahtooki. neehi-hsa noonki weelapici, neehi eelimihsahaaci.
en: He wanted to ride the buffalo. “I’ll ride this buffalo bull of mine by here any way you like”, rabbit told the women. And then he asked for a bridle, and then some spurs, and then a whip made of twisted rawhide. Then he asked for a saddle. And so then he put (the saddle) on. And then put the spurs on. Then he got on him and started him running.

mya: neehi-hsa paapakiciihkawaaci. niiyaaha peemihsaahaaci alenasooli mitemohsaki awiikawaanki. aapwe niiyaaha peepaamihsahaaci. neehi-hsa noonki šeekahwihsaawaaci atayali aayaahkaami. iiniinihsa wiiyoonkonci keekaanwitoontanoowaaci waapansooki.
en: He spurred him on. He rode the buffalo there past the women’s lodge. He kept passing by them there over and over again. And then his animal ran away into the bushes forever. That’s why rabbits have long heels.

mya: eehinki eehkwaapiikasici waapanswa.
en: That’s as far as rabbit goes.

mya: eeyeeliaeeyeelia ihsa peempaalici keewikawici.
en: Possum was walking around visiting.

mya: “šaaye kati nimaacaa, maalami piitaalhkwatwi.”
en: Then he said “It’s time for me to go home, it’s getting too cloudy.”

mya: neehi-hsa maacaaci. seekisici. “iihkipak-aalhkwatwi piiwi!” iišiteeheeci-hsa.
en: And he headed home. He was afraid. “A blue cloud is coming!” he thought.

mya: aapwalaapici. “hee”, iici-hsa, “nimpiiweetomaki ihsape”.
en: He looked back. “Hey!” he said, “It was only my fur”.

mya: aalhkwatwi pihkontee, “hee, nihtawaki-hsape”.
en: Then a dark cloud – “Ha!” he said, “It was only my ear”.

mya: “kineepikwa ninawinalikwa!” iišiteeheeta.
en: “A snake is chasing me!” he thought.

mya: maacaamwici. keeyapahtooki naante aalaankweeci. seekisici. seehkalwici. ansooyi wiiyoonkonci seehkalwici seekihekoci.
en: He ran away. He ran around until be became exhausted. He was frightened and slobbering. He was slobbering because he was frightened by his tail.

mya: meehci aašawišiweeci ansooyi amehkwali. aašawilaaci iiniini wiiyoonkonci seekihekoci.
en: Afterwards he traded off his tail to beaver. He traded it because it scared him.

mya: eehinki.
en: That’s the end.

mya: noohkoma akiili eehi teeši-mihtohseeniyowaki ciikaahkwe siipiiwi eehi katoohwaki teeši-mihtohseeniyowaaci. leni savannah iišiwiintamenki iiniini siipiiwi.
en: The place where my grandmother’s mother lived was near a river, in a place where the Cherokees lived. It was probably what people call the Savannah River.

mya: moohci ninkihkeelimaahsoo iiši-wiintinci noohkoma akiili. katoohwaki moohci ninkihkeelimaahsoo iiši-wiintaawaaci. ‘waapantaata’ iilaaciki myaamiaki, neehsinci wiiyoonkonci.
en: I don’t know what my grandmother’s mother was called. I don’t know what the Cherokees called her. The Myaamia called her ‘the Captive’ because she had been captured.

mya: myaamiaki ihsa neetopaliwaaci. niiyaaha-hsa meehkawaawaaci katoohwaahkwiali niišwi kwaaniswahi eehsaaci. eehkwi ntonamahwici anaapeemali eehkwanteeci kiimotenki awiiwali neehi aniicaanhsahi. kapootwe-hsa maacaaci kiikoo meelanki šaakoteeki. neehi-hsa neehpyaaci meeneehwilici. niiyaaha-hsa paahsamoowaaci pyaakimina. neehi-hsa ntopaliaki myaamiaki šaakosamoowaaci. ceekisamoowaaci ntaahswi tipeelintamilici.
en: The Myaamia were on the warpath. There they found a Cherokee woman who had two little girls. While her husband was away hunting, his wife and children were abducted. After a while, while he was heading home, he smelled something burning. Then, when he got there, they were gone. They had been there drying persimmons. The Myaamia warriors burned them. They burned up everything they owned.

mya: neehi-hsa weentamawaaci kiyošia katoohwahi: “kimotina niwiiwa neehi niniicaanhsaki!” meehci weentamaakiici, neehi-hsa maawatoontiiwaaci mihtohseeniaki. “ntoneehwaataawi”, iiwaacihsa. neehi-hsa maaciihkaawaaci weehsihkaawaaci katoohwaki neetoneehwaawaaci. neehi-hsa nihsokone peempaaliwaaci. neehihsa sakanki meehkawaawaaci mikihkooli. eenkihaminci-hsa. neehi-hsa kwaniswahi teehši eewalaawaaci myaamiaki ntopaliaki. aapweeyaaciki ooneeki neentoneehwaawaahpa.
en: And then the old man told the Cherokees: “Someone has taken my wife and children!” So then after he reported, the people held a meeting. “Let’s go after them!” they said. Then a large group of the Cherokees set off in search of them. So for three days they travelled. And then, after a while, they came across an old woman. She had been killed. The Myaamia warriors had taken only the girls. The search party returned home.

mya: myaamiaki neehpiilaawaaci ooneehi kwaniswahi. amihsima ihsa neepiki. neehi-hsa ooneeli neehsikohpanali ahšiimima kwaniswa keešiniikihekoci. neehi-hsa akimaanhsali weehkotamaakiilici awiiyawi kati akohšimaawilici. meehci-hsa neehsipici kiyošia, neehi-hsa eewalaaci eehi teeši-mihtohseeniwici. niiyaaha-hsa weeyaahkici.
en: The Myaamia brought the girls back. The elder sister died. And so the one who had captured the younger girl raised her as his own. Then the young chief asked for her, so that he could have a sister. After the old man consented, he took her to where he lived. There she stayed.

mya: neehi-hsa waayaahtanoohsali weehkotamaakolici awiiyawi išihka wiikimekoci. neehi-hsa waayaahtanoohsa miilinci. neehi-hsa eewalekoci waayaahtanonkiši. mihtami aniicaanhsali kwaniswali, ‘ceenkohšinka’, iilaawaaci-hsa. neehi-hsa kotakali eeniicaanhsiwaaci ‘peehkaahkosihkwa’. neehi-hsa aapooši kotakali eehsaawaaci, ‘mihtekihkwa’, iilaawaaci-hsa. neehi-hsa aapooši eehsaawaaci kotakali, ‘mihtekoonhsa’ iilaawaaci-hsa. neehi-hsa aapooši eehsaawaaci kotakali ‘waapaahkosihkwa’, iilaawaaci-hsa. iiniini-hsa eehinki ntaahswi aniicaanhsiwaaci.
en: And then a young Wea man asked for her in order to marry her. And so the young Wea man was given her. She was taken to Waayaahtanonki (Ouiatenon). Her first child was a girl who they called ‘Ceenkohšinka’. Then they had another, ‘Peehkaahkosihkwa’. And then they had another, called ‘Mihtekihkwa’. Then they had another one, called ‘Mihtekoonhsa’. And then they had another, and called her ‘Waapaahkosihkwa’. That was all the children they had.

mya: ceenkohšinka meehci keešiniikita weehšita. myaamiali eenaapeemita. neehi-hsa neešwaapaheeci. nkoti neepiki. neehihsa nkoti meehtohseeniwici. neehi-hsa ‘meesancihkwa’ iilaawaaci. keešiniikici iinaana. neehi-hsa weehšici. myaamiali eenaapeemici, ‘jocco godfrey’ iilinci-hsa. niišwi piloohsahi eehsaawaaci. nkotihsa ‘šinkohkwa’ iilinci. neehi kwiiwhsa ‘waapimaankwa’, iilincihsa. neehi-hsa waapimaankwa neepiki eehkwi apiilici. šinkohkwa ihsa weehšici. neehi-hsa yaalanwi piloohsahi eehsaaci. mihtami kwaniswali eeniicaanhsici ‘katani’ iilinta. nkoti ‘šowaapinamwa’ iilinta. nkoti ‘pakankia’ iilinta. nkoti ‘alensanaahkisamhkwa’ iilinta. nkoti ‘eeloonoonta’ iilinta. iiniiyenki ntaahswi eehsaaci piloohsahi šinkohkwa godfroy.
en: After Ceenkohšinka grew up, she got married. She married a Myaamia man. Then she had two children. One died. And one lived. And they called her ‘Meesancihkwa’. That one grew up. Then she got married. She married a Myaamia man called ‘Jocco Godfrey’. They had two children. One was called ‘Šinkohkwa’. And there was a boy who was called ‘Waapimaankwa’. Then Waapimaankwa died when he was still little. Šinkohkwa’ then got married. And then she had five children. The first one was a girl called ‘Katani’ (Katherine). One was called ‘Šowaapinamwa’. One was called ‘Pakankia’. One was called ‘Alensanaahkisamhkwa’. One was called ‘Eeloonoonta’. That was all the children Šinkohkwa Godfroy had.

mya: mihtekihkwa ihsa nihswi piloohsahi eehsaaci. amihsima ‘seekaahkweeta’ iilinci. neehi-hsa nkoti ‘seekaahkohkwa’ iilinci. neehi-hsa nkoti ‘waakaahkonanka’ iilinci. iiniinenki ntaahswi piloohsahi eehsaaci mihtekihkwa. seekaahkweeta ihsa nihswi piloohsahi eehsaaci. amihsima ‘mary ann’ iilinta. nkoti kwiiwhsa ‘neewanšimwa’ iilinta. neehi-hsa nkoti kwaniswa ‘seekotemhkwa’ iilinta. ooneehi nihswi mihtekoonhsa aniicaanhsahi: mihtekonhsehkwa, aciipihkihkwa, waapaahkosihkwa. mihtekonhsehkwa aniicaanhsahi: aahteehkanka, eeloonoonta, nkotikaapwa. waapaahkosihkwa aniicaanhsahi: wiikapimiša, mahkateehsipana, mihšahkatohkwa.
en: Mihtekihkwa then had three children. The oldest girl was called ‘Seekaahkweeta’. Then one was born called ‘Seekaahkohkwa’. And one was called ‘Waakaahkonanka’. That’s all the children Mihtekihkwa had. Seekaahkweeta then had three children. The oldest girl was called ‘Mary Ann’. One boy was called ‘Neewanšimwa’. And one girl was called ‘Seekotemhkwa’. These three were Mihtekoonhsa’s children: Mihtekonhsehkwa, Aciipihkihkwa, and Waapaahkosihkwa. Mihtekonhsehkwa’s children were Aahteehkanka, Eeloonoonta, and Nkotikaapwa. Waapaahkosihkwa’s children were Wiikapimiša, Mahkateehsipana, and Mihšahkatohkwa.

mya: neepihkiaki eehtookiki mankiiši ceekiši iihpinenki.
en: The Indian doctors had medicines for all kinds of diseases.

mya: paakicaahkwi ihsa eeyooki eehi paakisici. kahsikahsi iilahankiki kaahkikioni eeyonki eehi paakiciinki, neehi niiyaahi eehtookiki mankiiši. neehi-hsa mankiiši eešitahatooka. neehi-hkwa meeninki mankiišaapowi alaaminkonci iši-hka pilakiinki.
en: They would use the ague remedy where it was swollen. They would cut a bunch of little gashes using a razor where the swelling was, and they would put the medicine there. Then he would apply the medicine. Then one would drink the liquid medicine, to get well inside.

mya: kapootwe-hkwa šiipi neepilenciki eehkwi pilakiiwaahsiikwi. aalinta-hkwa kinšimi peelakiiciki. paakicaakani alaaminkiši iiyaaki ahpeehkwanemaanki. iini wiiyoonkonci keešiikileehseeciki.
en: Sometimes they would be treated for a long time before getting well. Some people would recover quickly. The belly swelling would spread into their ribs. Because of this they would come down with consumption.

mya: aalinta-hkwa neepihkiaki peelakiitookiki keešiikileehseenki. wiihsa neepihkiaki aalohkahankiki pilakiitoowaaci keešiikileehseenki. neehi-hkwa aalime eenkihiweeki.
en: Some of the doctors could cure consumption. Many doctors couldn’t cure consumption. then it was bound to be lethal.

mya: wiikapimiša akiili amehšoomali ihsa eeteehsiwilici, neehi-hsa kiihkayali meekaalikowaaci. wiihsa-hsa eenkihekowaaci kiihkayali. neehi-hsa aanikopia aalinta kiihkaya ašimaakaneehsiomahi weewiinkamihaaci. neehi-hsa niimaakani šeekwihtawaaci eehinki ciikaahkwe meehcakamiisi, eehi aweentioni wišihtoowaaci ciikaahkwe waapaahšiiki siipiiwi.
en: Wiikapimiša’s mother’s grandfather was a warrior and General Wayne was fighting them. Many of them were killed by General Wayne. Then Aanikopia defeated some of General Wayne’s soldiers. Then he captured the flag from him near where there was a small stream, where they had made peace near the Wabash River.

mya: wiikapimiša iilweeci iši-hka moohswaya meehcihpenalenci.
en: Wiikapimiša says this is how the deerskin is finished.

mya: niila nipi oonsaawicahkihkonki seekinamaani. niiyaaha eehtwaani moohswa antepi. neehi niiyaaha ceemonkahwaka moohswaya. nihsokone eekwincimaka, neehi peekwahwaka. meehci peehkwahwaki šeenkeekaholaka neehi naalahwaka nkotakone. neehi kiipookwaalaka, neehi eekolaka, neehi oonsaaswaka.
en: I pour the water into a brass kettle. There I put the deer’s brains. Then I put the deerskin in the water there. I soak it for three days and remove the hair from it. After I remove the hair from it, I stretch it and scrape it for one day. Then I sew the ends together and I hang it and cure it.

mya: šaaye noonki meehcihpenalaka. noonki kati wišihtwaani nimahkisena.
en: Now I’ve already finished treating it. Now I’ll make my moccasins.

mya: wiilinwa meehtišamaanki, peemihkiaanki, kaakaathkihkonki eehtwaanki, neehi weensamaanki.
en: When we finish cutting up the fat, we gather up the grease, put it in a kettle and boil it.

mya: meehtisamaanki waapicahkihkonki eehtwaanki. saahsikawaki eewakinci waapahaakani weešihtwaanki. neehi-hkwa miincipenki neepiswakinci.
en: When we finish cooking it, we put it in a tin can. We use the cracklings to make soap. and then we would cook (the cracklings) with some corn.

mya: neehi-hkwa koohkooša peehkahwakinci, apwaama neehi ateliaki neehi ahpehkwana teepantaakaninki eehtwaanki. neehi-hkwa weehkapahwakinci. neehi-hkwa meehci weehkapalicili eekolakinci. neehi-hkwa poohkicileenamaanki.
en: Then we would cut up the hog, and put the hams, shoulders, and ribs in a barrel. Then we salt it. And then, after it is finished salting, we hang it up. And then we smoke it.

mya: neehi-hkwa meehci oonsaasicili, eemwakinci.
en: Then, after it’s finished smoking, we eat it.

mya: koohsina eehinkiši meehceelimekwahki kiwiinsoonemi. niiloona neetaweelintamaanki, kitakimaayonemi pyaace.
en: Our father who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name.

mya: noowaaha kati išiliniaanki naapi išiliniyankwi koohsina eehinki peminki. miililoome noonki kaahkiihkwe miicioni eekami waapanki.
en: Thy kingdom come, thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread.

mya: aalawinamawiloome meeleewahki iihpinalilaanki, iši niiloona aalawinamawakinci meeleewahki iihpinašiaminkiki.
en: And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

mya: wiihkata meeleewahkionkiši awašihsooloome teehši meeleewahkionkonci piišiloome
en: Lead us not into temptation but deliver us from evil.
